text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a skin condition on your left dorsal hand; can you describe when you first noticed it and if the area is itchy, painful, or burning?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history; given your age and outdoor habits, does the lesion on your hand have a specific shape, color, or texture, and has it been changing in size or appearance recently? REQUEST IMAGES: Left dorsal hand clinical photos.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. The combination of your age, outdoor sun exposure, and the specific description of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand is classic for this precancerous skin lesion caused by cumulative UV damage. Given your history of diabetes, I will monitor this closely for changes, but the lack of pain or tenderness supports this benign yet pre-malignant diagnosis.
